edgeCasesAndExceptions: The four large islands are a physical-geography explanation, not a complete account of Japan's many smaller islands or a reason to erase remote and island communities.

Common region names are useful for orientation, travel, weather, language, and statistics, but their prefectural membership can vary by agency and purpose; they are not a universal local-government tier.
Japan has 47 prefectural-level governments, but their Japanese suffixes differ: Tokyo-to, Hokkaido-do, Kyoto-fu and Osaka-fu, and forty-three ken. English 'prefecture' is a convenient umbrella term.
Tokyo's 23 special wards are municipalities for many purposes; a ward in a designated city such as Nagoya is not the same governmental category and can function as a service-office subdivision.
National rules, prefectural administration, municipal procedures, school or employer policy, and private contracts must remain separate even when all are described using one place name.
Regional speech is not a binary split between one standard Japanese and one dialect per prefecture. Variation can cross borders and differ by generation, situation, identity, and community.
Ainu and Ryukyuan language varieties must not be flattened into novelty dialect examples. Official and scholarly classification language is sensitive, and some languages or varieties are endangered.
Climate and hazard exposure vary substantially by latitude, elevation, coast, and local terrain; national seasonal slogans do not replace current JMA information or local hazard maps.
Population, municipality counts, office names, administrative boundaries, and live emergency information change. The guide should link current official data rather than freeze unnecessary figures.
A glossary term declared in metadata is not meaningfully taught merely because an automatically rendered terminology list exists; useful terms should appear naturally in understandable prose.

scopeBoundaries: Do not present the guide as an encyclopedia, tourism ranking, cultural stereotype catalog, or replacement for focused legal and procedural guidance.
Do not add the guide as a mandatory journey step or create a one-article content group solely for visibility.
Do not imply that commonly used regions have one universal boundary or authority.
Do not imply that one dialect represents every speaker in a prefecture or that a newcomer must imitate local speech to integrate.
Do not hard-code volatile population, municipality-count, climate, or economic figures unless their edition and source are useful to the explanation.
Do not promote any article or assertion to reviewed status without explicit human editorial approval.
Do not treat a passing structural audit as substantive factual review.
Do not expand every Phase 13 finding in one implementation pass; separate structural repairs from factual and source corrections.
